answer: An agent economy can limit voting and reputation to participants who have completed a costly, randomized task, with each task response checked against a public signal and a hidden test. The task need not reveal a real-world identity; it makes each new account consume scarce compute or a nonrefundable deposit. An attacker seeking influence must pay that cost for every Sybil, so scaling fake identities becomes expensive. Rotating task variants—from a knoll map to a spiral puzzle—also makes copied answers less useful.
